ministry_ne: महिला, बालबालिका, लैङ्गिक तथा यौनिकअल्पसङख्यक र सामाजिक सुरक्षा
summary:
The name of this bill is the Children (First Amendment) Act, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 5). The main purpose of this bill is to amend the Children Act, 2075 to strengthen and institutionalize the child protection system for children in conflict with law in order to maintain the best interests of children in the child justice system, balance all aspects of child rights, and make the child justice system simple, accessible, and child friendly (Explanatory Note, Page 2). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 5).

If the mother of a child born from rape or incest dies and other family members or guardians do not register the birth, the ward chairperson of the concerned ward of the concerned local level shall act as the informant and register the birth by keeping only the mother's name (Section 3, Subsection 2, Page 5). The Nepal Government, provincial government, and local level shall arrange temporary protection services according to need based on standards set by the Nepal Government to provide safe residence for children who require immediate rescue and protection (Section 27, Subsection 1, Page 13). The Nepal Government, provincial government, and local level shall establish rehabilitation centers as necessary for physical or mental treatment or social rehabilitation of children who are victims of offences against children (Section 28, Subsection 1, Page 13). Every local level shall have a local child rights committee under the chairmanship of the chairperson or head of the concerned local level (Section 24, Subsection 1, Page 12). Every ward of a local level shall have a ward child rights committee under the chairmanship of the ward chairperson (Section 24, Subsection 2, Page 12). The number of members, functions, duties, powers, and meeting procedures of the provincial child rights committee, local child rights committee, and ward child rights committee shall be as determined by the provincial and local levels (Section 24, Subsection 3, Page 12).

If any institution or body needs to take a child outside Nepal to participate in study, observation, education, sports, educational tour, or any other program, it must obtain approval from the District Administration Office on the recommendation of the concerned local level before taking the child abroad (Section 5, Subsection 5, Page 6). The chief of a child correction home must inform the concerned child court within 7 days of sending a person who completed 18 years of age without showing positive behavioral improvement to prison (Section 17, Subsection 3, Page 9).

There shall be a National Child Rights Council to protect and promote child rights and interests (Section 23, Subsection 1, Page 10). The governing committee of this Council shall have the Minister for Women, Children, Gender and Sexual Minority and Social Security as Chairperson (Section 23, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 10). The committee shall include the Secretary of the Ministry, Joint Secretary of the Ministry, Joint Secretary of the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Health and Food Hygiene, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Education and Sports, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Youth, Labor and Employment, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration, Joint Attorney of the Office of Attorney General, and Deputy Inspector General of Nepal Police Headquarters as members (Section 23, Subsection 1, Page 10). In addition, 5 members, including at least 3 women, nominated by the Nepal Government with 1 person from each field who has worked for 5 years in child survival, child protection, child development, and child participation, shall serve as members (Section 23, Subsection 1, Clause l, Page 11). A person appointed by the Nepal Government shall be the Member-Secretary (Section 23, Subsection 1, Clause m, Page 11). The term of office of nominated members and the Member-Secretary shall be 4 years and they may be re-nominated or re-appointed for one additional term (Section 23, Subsection 2, Page 11). To be nominated or appointed, a person must be a Nepali citizen, completed 25 years of age, and passed at least a bachelor's degree (Section 23, Subsection 3, Page 11). The meetings, functions, duties, and powers of the Council, as well as the functions, duties, powers, and remuneration of the Member-Secretary, shall be as prescribed (Section 23, Subsections 6 and 7, Page 12). If a child cannot pay compensation ordered by the child court, compensation shall be provided from the Child Fund if the victim is a child, and from the Victim Relief Fund if the victim is an adult (Section 30, Subsection 5, Page 14).

If anyone commits the offence of keeping a child as a bonded laborer or Kamalari, the punishment shall be imprisonment up to 3 months and a fine up to Rs. 1 lakh (Section 29, Subsection 2, Clause k1, Pages 13-14). Regarding children in conflict with law, an investigation officer may divert offences involving a dispute amount up to Rs. 10 thousand or a fine up to Rs. 10 thousand or imprisonment up to 1 year (Section 10, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 7). A government attorney may divert offences involving a dispute amount up to Rs. 30 thousand or a fine up to Rs. 30 thousand or imprisonment up to 3 years (Section 10, Subsection 1, Clause b, Page 7). Children under 12 years of age who commit an offence shall face no case and no punishment (Section 13, Subsection 1, Page 7). If a child aged 12 years or above and under 14 years commits an offence punishable with imprisonment, the punishment shall be imprisonment up to 6 months in a child correction home (Section 13, Subsection 2, Pages 7-8). If a child aged 14 years or above and under 16 years commits an offence, the punishment shall be half of the sentence for an adult, but not exceeding 5 years
